_about: Alif (studied from 6 reference reels, the 'Sessions' interview look): soft teal cinematic grade, condensed serif captions in a tight translucent box that fill in word by word (sentence case, punctuation kept), a faint serif watermark, name tag with the title in an accent box and a hand-drawn arrow, editorial grid-paper collage cutaways (serif + accent-box keyword + marker notes), light-leak flashes between cutaways and the speaker. Accent: dark professional blue (the reference uses dark red). R1 port note: `music` is null here, not main's 'alif-match-a' - that id only exists in main's library/music/manifest.json, a Mixkit track this port deliberately does not bring over (BRANCH-AUDIT.md decision 4). `openFlash.clip` ('burn-04.mp4', from library/packs/editorsinventory/) is dropped for the same reason - this fork has no library/packs/ yet (decision 4 / E1, separate task) and pickBurn() dies on a missing file; without `clip` it falls back to the asset-free CSS-gradient flash.

director.style: Alif: calm, premium interview. Emphasis comes from editorial paper cutaways, not from caption effects.

scenes.paper: a grid-paper collage for the one key statement of each 15-20 s: 2-4 short lines; the key word in style 'box' (the accent box), one handwritten 'marker' note. 1.5-2.5 s. Lines are the speaker's own words.
scenes.window: only for a concrete thing the speaker describes that the audience should see. 1.5-3 s.

director.nametag: a name tag in the first 3 s: name + title
director.restraint: Keep the speaker on screen most of the time. Never two cutaways back to back.
